title: Onboard evidence snapshot and skill-gating ladder
content:
Purpose:
This working doc proposes a compact, evidence-driven onboarding and early-signal assessment framework we can use across engineering and product hires. Goal is to reduce subjectivity in 15/30/60 decisions and create a lightweight gate ladder where mentors and managers can mark concrete outcomes.

Summary (one-liner):
Create repeatable 15/30/60 evidence snapshots and a 4-step skill-gating ladder (Orientation -> Build-first -> Ownership -> Impact) with explicit artifacts, examples, and pass/fail guidance. Use for new hires, internal role changes, and compact contractor-to-perm trials.

Why this:
- Too many early ramp conversations are purely anecdotal or rely on status updates.
- We need a small set of observable deliverables managers can agree on quickly.
- Should work with remote hires and cross-pool rotations where mentors vary.

Key constraints and design choices:
- Keep lightweight: each gate should be decidable within a 30-minute sync + 15-min review of artifacts.
- Evidence-first: prefer tangible artifacts (PRs, runbooks, demo videos, design sketches) rather than impressions.
- Use a 3-point scorer per competency (0 = not demonstrated, 1 = emerging, 2 = reliable).
- Allow mentor and manager separate signals; escalation when signals diverge by >2 points.

The 4-step Skill-Gating Ladder (short):
1) Orientation (week 0–2): onboarding rituals, infra access, small read/modify tasks.
   - Core evidence: working dev environment, completed security checklist, first tiny PR (README or doc fix) merged, short intro demo to team.
   - Success threshold: 3 of 4 artifacts present; at least one reviewer comment addressed.

2) Build-first (week 2–6): shipping a scoped, reviewer-validated change and owning follow-ups.
   - Core evidence: a scoped feature/bug PR (<= 5 files changed), CI green, unit/integration tests added or updated, issue/bug triage notes.
   - Success threshold: PR merged + 1 post-merge bug/feedback owned and resolved or triaged.

3) Ownership (week 6–12): proactively improving an area, cross-team communication, on-call readiness signals.
   - Core evidence: ownership doc or runbook updates, at least one incident postmortem contribution or production debug story, direct cross-team async threads with action items.
   - Success threshold: documented improvement and two stakeholder acknowledgments (Slack threads or ticket comments).

4) Impact (week 12+): measurable product or infra impact, mentoring newer hires, and leading retrospectives.
   - Core evidence: a measurable metric change attributed to work (perf, latency, user metric), a guided onboarding session for a new hire, or a design doc driving a roadmap ticket.
   - Success threshold: 1 metric-linked improvement OR mentoring session + roadmap artifact.

15/30/60 evidence snapshot templates (one-page each):
- 15-day snapshot (brief):
  * Quick status (green/amber/red)
  * 3 artifacts + links: ENV OK, first PR link, onboarding q&a notes
  * Mentor notes (2–3 bullets): blockers, confidence level, recommended focus next 15 days
  * Decision cue: continue / accelerate / pair-up / re-scope

- 30-day snapshot (brief):
  * Status + competency scores (Code, Systems, Communication): 0/1/2
  * Deliverables list (PRs, docs) with short outcome line for each
  * Manager and mentor independent recommendation (agree/disagree)
  * Decision cue: proceed to Build-first or extend pairing focus by 2 weeks

- 60-day snapshot (brief):
  * Status + expanded competency grid (adds Ownership, Reliability)
  * Impact indicators (bug counts, review velocity, code quality notes)
  * Pass/hold/accelerate decision with evidence lines (what to show at 90d)

Scorecard example (single row per competency):
- Competency: System design
- Mentor score: 1
- Manager score: 2
- Evidence: review comments on design PR (#345), design doc draft link
- Resolution: set two concrete follow-ups (read chapter X, pair on design next week)

Guidance for raters (mentor and manager):
- Use artifacts as primary signal. If you rely on subjective impressions, call out why and list three observable behaviors that justify it.
- When mentor and manager diverge by 2+ points, schedule a 30-min calibration: walk artifact list and align on minimum pass criteria.
- If candidate/hire is remote and timezone-limited, accept asynchronous demos (short Loom videos) as valid artifacts.

Templates (copy-paste for Slack/PR):
- 15-day Slack update stub: "15d snapshot: ENV OK; first PR merged: <link>; blocker: missing gcp role; mentor rec: pair on infra next wk"
- Calibration prompt (email): "Please review artifacts linked below and flag any missing context before the calibration sync: [links]."

Mentor playbook (must be short):
- Day 0–7: confirm dev env; introduce 3 core contacts; watch first PR + give 2 actionable comments
- Week 2–6: pair 2x/week on domain tasks; ensure PRs are scoped to reviewer time; show how to triage a bug
- Week 6–12: shift to async check-ins; encourage ownership doc + stakeholder outreach

Fail/Remediation lanes (what to do if evidence not present):
- Missing Orientation artifacts: immediate unblock plan (IT ticket + buddy pairing) — 7 day remediation window
- Missing Build-first progress by week 6: re-scope tasks + mandate daily pairing for 2 weeks, re-evaluate at week 8
- Major capability mismatch at any gate: move to formal review (HR + people-ops + hiring manager) with documented improvement plan or transition options (contract extension, role change, offboarding)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether scorecard is saved to Confluence (yes) or stored on private hiring drive (privacy concerns). See CON-2421.
- Should we make the score thresholds role-specific (e.g., IC-4 vs IC-2)? proposal: keep core ladder consistent but allow role-specific sample artifacts.
- Build a tiny 1-click snapshot generator in Console for managers (low priority).

Appendix: sample micro-evidence list (short):
- Dev env screenshot with uname + node/npm versions
- First PR + 1 reviewer comment example
- Loom screencast (3–5m) explaining a recent change
- Runbook edit diff + short note on why changed

Slack-ish notes to self (choppy):
- Priya: want this to be lightweight for fast hires (growth roles)
- Marco: add triage rubric for buggy PRs (severity bucketization)
- TODO: link to hiring rubric templates in hiring-catalog repo

— end of draft —

Notes: put this under shared_drives/company/misc and flag to people-ops for a 1hr sync. I want to trial on 2 upcoming hires (infra eng + analyst) and iterate.
